Volos Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Volos, Greece

Demolished. Volos was home to a small Romaniot Jewish community — one of Greece's ancient, Greek-speaking Jewish populations, distinct from Sephardic or Ashkenazi communities — as early as the 14th century, growing substantially after 35 families from the Peloponnese resettled here in the early 1800s. Rabbi Moshe Pesach served the community for an extraordinary 63 years, from 1892 until his death in 1955, and by 1930 the population had peaked around 2,000. Most of the remaining Jews were deported via Larissa to the death camps in March 1944, though the community was rebuilt afterward and grew into one of Greece's largest, after Athens and Salonika.
